Seeking Alpha analyst Seeking Profits noted that there has been an increasing divergence between the performance of consumer stocks and the performance of consumers. Consumers have weathered a substantial inflation shock surprisingly well this year, aided by the fact the labor market has strengthened in 2026.

“With ongoing labor market momentum, I believe the consumer can keep chugging along, though an acceleration is unlikely. Given high oil and borrowing costs, markets are skeptical the consumer can hold up as well as I believe, driving the sector lower. I increasingly see this as an opportunity to add beaten-up, quality stocks as macro data is likely to hold in better than feared over the next 12-18 months,” the analyst said.

“The beauty category has been a bright spot in recent months as consumer spending holds in better than feared and travel activity persists. With ongoing market share gains and capacity to grow locations, Ulta is a growth company on the offensive. Earnings remain strong, and with winning brand partnerships and a resilient consumer, Ulta is set up well for continued growth, meaning this rally may have room to run,” Seeking Profits said.

“Best Buy is a rare standout among companies selling “big ticket items.” We have seen weakness across higher-cost goods (i.e., appliances, autos, etc.) as consumers defer purchases in this affordability environment. The weakness in housing and autos may actually be helping BBY, as that creates more room in budgets to splurge on electronics. With new potential products around AI poised to hit stores, Best Buy’s standout growth may be set to continue through 2027,” the analyst noted.

was moved to a neutral rating at BofA after Barry Diller's People Inc. withdrew its takeover bid. However, shortly after, a report indicated that MGM was discussing making an offer for the latter to likely buy back a large chunk of its shares.

“MGM shares fell after Barry Diller backed away from his efforts to acquire the company, which likely would have required a substantial increase in debt. This may be a canary-in-the-coal-mine moment of how the substantial rise in rates can act as a stumbling block for debt-fueled M&A. The rumored MGM purchase of PPLI could be an attractive way to reduce MGM’s share count by a quarter while leaving its balance sheet on solid footing. As such, I view this pullback as creating an interesting opportunity for investors,” as per Seeking Profits.

lost over 30% in the quarter after reporting underwhelming earnings in July. The stock was downgraded by Bank of America to Underperform from Buy, with analysts arguing that the pest-control company's weaker-than-expected second-quarter results have reduced confidence in a near-term recovery in residential demand. In September, Piper Sandler also cut to neutral from overweight due to concerns arising from agentic AI and private equity investment in the pest control space, which appears to favor small/local pest control providers over national companies.

“Rollins shares have now lost about half of their value over the past year, and yet they still trade about 25x earnings. The stock has been priced for perfection, and with weakness in home sales, that was not justified. Low churn in the housing market reduces the opportunity to sell new pest services, and ongoing affordability challenges likely have consumers delaying discretionary treatments. With the housing market unlikely to improve, competition fierce, and valuation high, this is not a dip to buy,” the analyst added.

With the earnings season kicking off in October, investors will keenly watch out for the sector’s overall performance. They will also keep an eye out for consumer spending patterns as we tread closer to the holiday season amid a volatile economic backdrop.
